$comment: Hospitals a Greater Manchester crew conveys to, with the capabilities dispatch actually routes on. Every non-identity field is an evidence record — value / confidence / sources / note — and 'unknown' is a shipping value: the sim treats it as not available rather than guessing. Ten in-patch EDs as before, plus RMCH (the paediatric MTC, campus-shared with MRI), the two GM sites with no ED (Trafford, Rochdale) so routing can be honest about them, and four out-of-patch destinations the network edges need (Preston, Aintree, Whiston, Macclesfield). Researched and adversarially checked 2026-09-05; see data/research/ambulance/hospitals_research.md for the unverified list.

network.note: GMMTN v4.0: 'the Major Trauma Centre function is provided by a collaborative which comprises Manchester Royal Infirmary (MRI)... Salford Royal Hospital (SRH)'. GM does not have two independent MTCs; it has one MTC function delivered by a two-site collaborative.
network.reviewNote: Four successive peer reviews between 2014 and 2024 found GM non-compliant with national major trauma standards. NHS Greater Manchester is running a site-selection study to choose a single specialist site; as of 2026 it is still undecided. Two MTC sites are modelled today and the designation is flagged as provisional.

ed.note: Adult ED; paediatric emergencies go to Royal Manchester Children's Hospital on the same campus (H-RMCH).

trauma.note: One of the two sites of the GM Major Trauma Centre Collaborative. GMMTN v4.0: the NWAS GM pathfinder directs all penetrating injury trauma, thoraco-abdominal / suspected vascular injury, isolated penetrating thoracic injury, pregnant >20 weeks with head injury, and suspected isolated hepatic trauma to MRI.

ppci.note: 24/7 primary PCI is stated in MFT catheter-lab recruitment adverts, not a service specification. A 2017 Royal Oldham protocol described an in-hours/out-of-hours rota with a 17:30 handover; nine years stale. Do not ship any hotline numbers.

stroke.note: District Stroke Centre per the GMNISDN local stroke units page dated 12 Jul 2022 — the sole source for the DSC list. Does not take hyperacute stroke.

neuro.note: Adult neurosurgery for GM is at Salford Royal; paediatric at RMCH.

cardiothoracic.note: GMMTN routes isolated penetrating thoracic injury directly to the MRI cardiothoracic team.

helipad.note: Elevated pad on the roof of the Grafton Street multi-storey car park, MFT Oxford Road campus, linked by a high-level transfer corridor: under 3 min to the MRI ED, under 6 min to the RMCH paediatric ED. Opened to patients 10 May 2021; £3.9m, £1.36m of it HELP Appeal. Projected ~300 airlifts/yr; actual 197 landings in the first two years. Night landing clearance could not be established — the '24-hour access' phrasing refers to the link bridge, not night flying.

offSiteHls.note: Before the pad opened, air ambulances landed in Platt Fields Park about a mile away and patients were transferred by road. Single trade-press source (Architects' Journal). Whether it was daylight-only is unverified.

burns.note: The British Burn Association listing (20 Oct 2017) records RMCH under Paediatrics as a 'Burn Service', not a 'Burn Centre'. MFT markets it as a Centre. The dispatch consequence is the same: a badly burned child goes to Oxford Road.

ed.note: Paediatric emergencies seen in the Panda Unit up to the 16th birthday.

trauma.note: One of the two sites of the GM Major Trauma Centre Collaborative, and home of the purpose-built Greater Manchester Major Trauma Hospital (opened May 2024). GMMTN v4.0: cranial trauma with GCS <12 goes directly to Salford Royal via the supplementary Pathfinder; the collaborative describes it as taking 'nine out of ten' GM major trauma patients — a service claim, not a measured statistic. Alternative TTL number 0161 206 5354.

stroke.note: The Comprehensive Stroke Centre for Greater Manchester: 24/7 hyperacute admissions and, since March 2022, 24/7 mechanical thrombectomy. Takes every GM hyperacute stroke outside the ASCs' 06:45–22:45 hours.

helipad.note: Rooftop pad on the Greater Manchester Major Trauma Hospital building with a dedicated lift shaft to the ED. £2m HELP Appeal, first instalment presented 11–12 April 2022. Structure completed October 2022; operational with the hospital — the June 2024 date is press inference from '117 landings in two years' reported 1 June 2026, not an NHS commissioning date. Anticipated ~360 landings/yr; actual ~58. OSM tags lit=no but the same record calls an aluminium deck 'paved' — near-zero weight. Physical limits are from one anonymous OSM edit: uncertain.

offSiteHls.note: Before the rooftop pad, air ambulance patients landed on a nearby sports field 'less than half a mile away' — the distance is Dr Beattie quoted by NWAA, not an institutional measurement. No source names the field.

value.paediatricNote: UNKNOWN. MFT's 2020 notice diverting paediatric emergencies to RMCH is still live on the trust site with no published reopening, while MFT's Wythenshawe children's services page describes a working five-bay department. The trust's own pages contradict each other. Do not route a child here until MFT confirms.

helipad.note: Helicopters are observed landing on site (video evidence, but of the Children's Air Ambulance, a different charity from NWAA). Every specific — 'ground-level asphalt pad at 53.3884, -2.2896' — traces to a single OurAirports record GB-0344 last updated 28 June 2016, republished by UK Airfield Guide, PilotNav, AirportMap and a flight-sim scenery pack, and copied into OSM way 1218638533 which carries ref=GB-0344. That is one 2016 crowd-sourced source, not four. Listed by the HELP Appeal under PLANNED A&E helipads, which at Royal Preston meant an upgrade-to-compliance of an existing pad, not a new build. NOT an NWAA air destination.
